page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, virtualized on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor operating up to 4.2 GHz. It is provisioned with 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with two threads per core, 480 MB of shared L3 cache, and 192.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware accelerators for advanced matrix calculations and cryptographic operations include AVX-512, AMX-TILE, AMX-INT8, and VAES. Direct graphics acceleration is absent, but the configuration includes 2832 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark evaluations position the D48ds_v7 in the top 25 percent across multiple memory throughput, data processing, and enterprise execution tests. Uncached large-block read operations register at 259.05 GB/sec, complemented by a cached small-block read bandwidth of 3733.43 GB/sec. Synthetic CPU testing reflects a PassMark score of 68963.55 alongside 52573.11 in cryptographic routines. High-concurrency performance remains elevated, evidenced by 84.18 million Redis SET operations per second and static web transfer rates of 72.52 GB/sec. CPU-driven inference benchmarks for lightweight machine learning models deliver 239.1 prompt tokens per second and 28.93 generation tokens per second using a medium 7-billion-parameter model.

Resource allocation provides high local storage capacity and substantial CPU density within a single node, minimizing the necessity of multi-instance distributed overhead. The bundled fast NVMe storage alleviates external block storage bottlenecks for temporary data pipelines, caching tiers, and high-frequency read-write loads. However, compute workloads relying on non-matrix vectorized parallelization or graphics acceleration may find limitations without discrete GPUs, and synthetic compute benchmarks via stress-ng measure within the middle 50 percent of tested instances.

The D48ds_v7 functions effectively for transaction-heavy relational databases, large-scale Redis in-memory caches, data compression routines, enterprise web serving layers, and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference pipelines requiring rapid access to local storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores) based on the Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Supported by 192.0 GB of system memory and 480 MB of L3 cache, it features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX matrix extensions. The configuration integrates 2832 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and lacks discrete GPUs. In synthetic and operational benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier results in uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 259.05 GB/sec, along with 84.18 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark computational figures. The presence of dense local NVMe storage combined with a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio yields strong qualitative resource efficiency for high-IOPS applications. The instance is suited for enterprise relational databases, large in-memory caching systems, high-traffic web backends, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks.
